147.80514,-31.29552.type: Cotton (Gossypium hirsutum L.), licensed field trial
147.80514,-31.29552.desc: WHAT. A licensed GMO crop field trial site, Herbicide tolerance and insect resistance, held by Monsanto Australia Pty Ltd. WHERE IT SITS. OGTR named the council area this site is in and published no coordinate on the page this was read from, so this marker sits in that council area and not at the trial itself. WHY IT MATTERS. OGTR names the council area of every licensed site, its area in hectares and the licence it runs under. No other register on this map states where a release is at all, which is the comparison worth making even at this resolution.

-72.92505,41.30821.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Part of Alexion Pharmaceuticals, Inc.. -2.99902,53.40761.name: Care Fertility Liverpool
-2.99902,53.40761.state: 8, Princes Dock Pier Head, Liverpool, L3 1DL
-2.99902,53.40761.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-79.38492,43.65760.name: Douglas Hospital Research Centre
-79.38492,43.65760.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, September 2023
-79.38492,43.65760.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, September 2023. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

153.01400,-27.49900.name: Wolbachia — World Mosquito Program
153.01400,-27.49900.desc: Releases mosquitoes carrying Wolbachia so the population becomes unable to transmit dengue, across more than a dozen countries, with published trials showing large reductions in cases. It is the most successful large-scale insect release programme anywhere and involves no genetic engineering at all — and every argument that engineering was the only available route has to account for it.

-94.12000,36.33000.name: Cobb-Vantress (Tyson Foods)
-94.12000,36.33000.desc: One of two companies supplying the breeding stock behind essentially every broiler chicken raised on Earth, owned by the largest US meat processor. Roughly 70 billion chickens are slaughtered worldwide each year and the genetics of almost all of them trace to Cobb or Aviagen. That is a tighter concentration than seed, medicine or any other facet on this map, and it attracts a fraction of the attention: a breeding decision made in Arkansas reaches nearly every commercial flock in the world within a few generations, and there is no alternative supplier to switch to.

-2.24500,53.47700.name: Wildlife Incident Investigation Scheme
-2.24500,53.47700.desc: Report a dead wild animal, pet or bee colony you believe was poisoned by pesticide, and the state collects the carcass and pays for the analysis. Results are published annually and feed into whether an approval is kept. It is one of very few schemes anywhere where a member of the public triggers a laboratory test at public expense rather than their own, and the reason it matters here is that herbicide-tolerant crops exist to be sprayed — the spraying is the part with a body count.

-106.31310,42.86660.name: Heliospect Genomics
-106.31310,42.86660.state: Registered in Wyoming — operating from the United States
-106.31310,42.86660.desc: A company selling polygenic scoring of embryos, exposed in October 2024 by an advocacy group's undercover recordings and reporting alongside them. On those recordings staff described ranking up to a hundred embryos on predicted intelligence, sex, height, obesity risk and risk of mental illness, at a price reported as up to fifty thousand dollars for a hundred embryos and around four thousand for fewer, and said several couples had already selected embryos this way. The company says it operates within all applicable law, and it does. Three things make this the entry this facet needed. Selecting embryos on predicted high intelligence is prohibited in the United Kingdom and permitted in the United States, so the same test is legal or not depending on where the clinic is. Its predictions were reported as drawing on a publicly funded British genetic database open to approved health research in the public interest. And its application to that database described improving prediction of complex traits without disclosing embryo screening as an intended commercial use.
